stem.text: The amount of water in a storage tank changes at the rate \( A'(t) = 10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{5} \right)} + 5 \) gallons per hour for \( 0 \le t \le 10 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 140 gallons of water in the tank, and t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find the time in \( 0 \le t \le 10 \) at which the amount A(t) of water is greatest, and justify the answer. Show the setup for the calculations.

answer_key.label: The amount is greatest at t = 10, where A is 190 gallons, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at both critical points and at t = 10.

worked_solution.text: The amount is \( A(t) = 140 + \int_{0}^{t} \left(10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi s}{5} \right)} + 5\right)\,ds \), so \( A'(t) = 10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{5} \right)} + 5 \). Setting \( A'(t) = 0 \) and solving with a calculator gives \( t = 3.333 \) and \( t = 6.667 \) in the interval.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points of an accumulation function

worked_solution.text: The candidates are the critical points and both endpoints: \( A(0) = 140 \), \( A(3.333) \approx 170.450 \), \( A(6.667) \approx 159.550 \), and \( A(10) = 140 + \int_{0}^{10} A'(s)\,ds = 190 \).
The largest candidate value is 190, at the endpoint, so the amount is greatest at \( t = 10 \) hours.
